frontier.hypothesis: The goto basin's single extra instruction is removable by an ordinary-C spelling of the inner loop's exit test that defeats cse2's merge of the signed `lh` with the next iteration's unsigned `lhu` of the same address.
frontier.mechanism: cse2 sees `lh $v0,0($s0)` in the test block and `lhu $v1,0($s0)` at the top of the body and, because only the low 16 bits are consumed (the value is immediately `sh`-stored into rect[0]), replaces the lhu with `move $v1,$v0`. dbr then uses that move as the bgez delay filler instead of `sll $v0,$s1,5`, which is displaced to the top of the body, and the load-delay `nop` after the `lh` becomes the net +1. Target performs no such merge: it emits both loads and puts the sll in the delay slot.
frontier.next_probe: SYNTHESIS modality on memory/grind/func_80041BF4/goto_basin_best.c (40 @ 136) as the base. Try spellings that change what cse2 sees rather than what the values are: read the test value through a differently-typed lvalue than rect[0]'s source, read rect[0]'s source BEFORE the test in program order, spell the test as `if (tbl[0] < 0) goto done;` at the top of the body, and make the test read `*tbl` while rect[0] reads `tbl[0]` (or vice versa). Read the `.cse2` dump for the merge decision in each case (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80041BF4) rather than only the score - the score in this basin is dominated by the callee-save permutation and will not move monotonically. Track INSN COUNT (needs 135) as the primary signal.

frontier.hypothesis: The goto basin's callee-save permutation (xoff=$s8 yoff=$s7 r=$s5 g=$s4 fp_ptr=$s6 vs target's xoff=$s5 yoff=$s4 r=$s7 g=$s6 fp_ptr=$fp) is driven by global.c's allocno priority ordering, not by any source-level lever.
frontier.mechanism: s9 measured every declaration-order permutation inert in this basin (43 across the board), which rules out the s1/s3 lever that worked in the while basin. What orders the s4..s8 pool must therefore be allocno priority (live length x reference count), which the goto spelling changes because it changes every LUID in the function.
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS modality. Dump `.greg` for the goto basin and for the while-basin candidate side by side (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80041BF4 on each) and read the `;; N regs to allocate` list, each allocno's priority, and the conflict sets for the pseudos holding xoff/yoff/r/g/fp_ptr. The question to answer with numbers is WHICH quantity differs between the two basins for those five pseudos - live length, n_refs, or the order they enter the allocation loop. Do not propose another source-level rotation lever until that number is in hand; s9 already measured the obvious ones dead.

frontier.hypothesis: The trailing `func_8003E2A0() == 1` test has an ordinary-C spelling that puts the rematerialised literal 1 in $t0 rather than $v1, closing the last 2 instructions without the `one` constant-holder (carried unchanged from s8).
frontier.mechanism: Reload rematerialises the REG_EQUIV (const_int 1) into a spill register; which one it picks is a function of the spill-reg ordering at that point. s4 measured three spellings inert (block-local rc, function-scope rc, Yoda) and s8 proved the choice is independent of the loop residual (worth exactly 2 in BOTH basins), so the remaining space is the SHAPE of the test itself, not where its result is named.
frontier.next_probe: SYNTHESIS modality.
